still_open: a complete counted scalar-AArch64 implementation of the step is NOT claimed here; the priced rows are analytic instruction bounds grounded in the named operation sequences, which tracks/docs/COST_MODEL.md explicitly permits.
what_replaces_it: an itemised static row of 290 insn/step (263 walk rows + 27 insert rows, ledger_v13.ROWS and ROWS_INSERT), each row a named sequence of scalar AArch64 operations, plus a second price that charges one FULL reference unit per random table access (claim_at_1ref_access) so no bound in the package rests on the cheap row.
why: v12's scripts/exec_count.py incremented counters inside fold loops that did not perform the folds and reduced with Python's arbitrary-width `% p`; its 227 insn/step figure was therefore a shell, as verdict 2620b615 point 2 states. v13 WITHDRAWS that row rather than restating it.
